newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawians to decide again on death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Malawians to decide again on death penalty.

text.p: The Malawi cabinet on Wednesday agreed that human rights group Amnesty International should help conduct a survey on whether Malawians want the death penalty abolished, three years after saying they wanted to retain it.
Amnesty International has offered to send representaives to Malawi as soon as government gave the go-ahead.

The Malawi parliament two years ago voted in favour of retaining the death penalty, and a national survey conducted a year earlier showed the majority of Malawians, particulary those from rural areas, favoured capital punishment.
But the constitution, instituted by the new multi-party government after 30 years of single-party rule, also says no inhuman or cruel and degrading punishment should be inflicted on any person.
Law Commissioner Elton Singini told Reuters the retention of the death penalty created problems for Malawi.

"For a country with a death penalty ... it is not possible to obtain extradition of fugitive offenders from countries without death penalties. And Malawi in particular has several such cases pending," he said.
Singini said it was possible to abolish the death penalty by simply changing the statute books without necessarily amending the constitution, which requires a referendum.
